title: Around the World on a Bicycle
summary: The first person to cycle round the world, on a high-wheeled penny-farthing with no gears and solid tyres: across the American West, Europe, Turkey and Persia, then India, China and Japan. The bikepacking pioneer.

sources.label: Berkhamsted Local History: Thomas Stevens crosses America by bicycle
Scroll.in: India through the eyes of the first round-the-world cyclist

approximate: Main places from his book; the roads between them are approximate.

stops.name: San Francisco
stops.text: Off from San Francisco on a 50-inch Columbia high-wheeler, with a change of socks and a revolver.

stops.name: The Rockies
stops.text: Across the Sierra and the deserts, often pushing the bike along railway tracks.

stops.name: Chicago
stops.text: Over the plains to the Great Lakes.

photo.credit: File:Chicago River ferry.jpg: John Picken derivative work: Georgfotoart

stops.name: Boston
stops.text: About 3,700 miles and 103 days after San Francisco, much of it pushed on foot: the first crossing of America by bicycle. He then decided to keep going round the world.

stops.name: Vienna
stops.text: Across England, France and Germany to the Danube.

stops.name: Constantinople
stops.text: Through the Balkans to the Bosphorus.

stops.name: Anatolia
stops.text: Across Anatolia, where crowds gathered to see the strange machine.

stops.name: Tehran
stops.text: Winter in Persia as a guest of the Shah's court. Refused passage through Afghanistan, he turned back.

stops.name: India
stops.text: By sea to India, then riding the Grand Trunk Road.

stops.name: China
stops.text: A hard, sometimes hostile ride through southern China.

stops.name: Yokohama
stops.text: Across Japan to Yokohama, the end of the first ride round the world by bicycle.
